name: Netherlord
reason: The source rank 'Demon King' was renamed 'Netherlord' to give the apex demon tier a darker Western fantasy register and avoid confusion with royal titles.
description: Netherlord is the apex rank of the demon race, reserved for its most powerful members; even the imperial army treats taking one down as a major feat, and one could crush Zane with a flick of a finger (Ep 137). Netherlords such as Aldrich and Porter drive the great war arc around Eps 125-145, with Porter said to have destroyed Tronson. Per the master sheet, Orion is explicitly not a Netherlord.

name: Netherlord Aldrich
reason: The source's title-name 'Black Iron Demon King' was localized as a personal name, 'Aldrich', under the rank 'Netherlord', fitting the adaptation's Western naming for major demon antagonists.
description: A Netherlord and major antagonist of the war arc (Eps 133-140), one of the Four Dreadlords, who wields the Sacred Flame. In Ep 138 he confronts Zane on the battlefield, thundering commands and probing the defiant youth's ambitions with mingled malice and curiosity. He corresponds to the source's Black Iron Demon King, who is nearly invincible so long as he holds the Sacred Fire and whose fire Luo Zheng absorbs during the battle at White Emperor City.

name: Caleb
issues: Surface name 'Caleb' covers three different characters: Caleb of House Warrick = source Wang Hengzhi (Eps 30-91), Caleb Preston, a sect prodigy devoted to Cora (Eps 729-730), and Caleb Garrett, scion of a mine-owning clan (Ep 1057). Also, the master sheet calls Caleb 'Adrian's brother' while Ep 88 calls Adrian Warrick the only son and heir of House Warrick.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Caleb' was chosen for the arrogant young noble, and the surname 'Warrick' ties him to House Warrick (source: the Wang family).
description: A young noble of House Warrick and early antagonist (Eps 30-91), close to Perrin, whom he orders against Zane during the sect examination and shields thereafter. After Zane shatters Perrin's Energy Channels, Caleb moves to avenge him but, despite his Level Two Life Force cultivation, is paralyzed by Adrian's suffocating aura (Eps 89-91). Matches source Wang Hengzhi, the young master who protects Luo Peiran and is cowed by his elder sibling Wang Yanmiao's pressure.

name: Black Star
reason: The source item 'Black Star Pickaxe' kept its name, with 'Black Star' as the artifact's proper name and 'pickax(e)' used as a descriptor in the episodes.
description: A legendary pickaxe recorded in the Dragon-blooded annals, a supreme artifact bearing three ten-star divine runes in the source. Zane pursues it from Ep 855 onward because it is the only tool capable of digging heartstones out, and it becomes the prize every faction in the arc is chasing (Eps 855-869).

name: Flaming Place
reason: The source 'Flame Demon Sacred Ground', one of the demons' twin sacred grounds, was simplified to 'Flaming Place' to pair with 'Dread Place' in the adaptation's plainer naming for the Ogres' territories.
description: One of the two peak sixth-grade sanctuaries held by the Ogres, a territory dotted with thousands of active volcanoes of every size, which is why they call it the Flaming Place (Ep 628). Together with its twin, the Dread Place, it schemes for dominance and finally declares open war on the Violet Heart Sanctuary, marching Soul Sea Realm masters toward its territory (Eps 627+). It corresponds to half of the source's Twin Demon Holy Land.

name: House Moon
reason: The source 'Mo Family' was localized as 'House Moon', turning the surname Mo into the English 'Moon' under the show's 'House X' convention for noble families.
description: A declining noble house in the northern part of the city, once a Great House, whose family tree boasts the legend Jack Moon (Eps 177-200). It is Ethan and Yates's family, headed by James Moon; even in decline its butler sneers at mere outer disciples, and its gatherings remain major social events. Matches the source Mo Clan, a lukewarm noble family whose income depends on a few mines.

name: Hall
issues: 'the Hall' is a context-dependent short form, not a distinct entity: it refers to Cloud Hall in Eps 309-448 (Kenneth, Eddy, Alan contexts) and to the Karma Hall trial site in Eps 1263-1291 (iron ticket, mountain rules). Because the referent differs by episode range it cannot be aliased to a single canonical.

name: Fighting Soul Realm
reason: The source soul stage, rendered variously as 'Battle Soul Realm', 'War Soul Realm' and 'Combat Soul Realm' in translation, was standardized as 'Fighting Soul Realm' in the adaptation.
description: A rare soul-cultivation stage in which the soul itself can be used directly in battle; it is a trial of will that even late Inner-Core and Spirit-Tribulation masters may never pass (Ep 445). Zane's soul enters the Fighting Soul Realm in the upper world, placing him in an entirely different category of existence, making his soul his greatest weapon and rendering him immune to soul attacks such as the Skull Ghost Hand (Eps 462-501).

name: Stellar Body
reason: The source divine art 'Stellar Battle Body' was shortened to 'Stellar Body' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A transcendent body-cultivation divine art that must be trained under the starry night, borrowing gravity and power from the stars, even slingshotting consciousness across the void (Eps 572-600). Zane cultivates it alongside his Tapestry of Sun, Moon, and Stars, connecting with additional stars more easily as his grasp of the laws deepens (Ep 1129); in the source it shows its full power only after the nine stars of the Spiritual Pedestal Realm are opened.

name: Seven Great Houses
issues: Name drift: Eps 71-149 also use 'Seven Ruling Families' for the same source 'seven great families'; the two variants overlap in Eps 100-149 (e.g. Ep 100 says 'Seven Great Houses' and Ep 101 'Seven Ruling Families') before 'Seven Great Houses' becomes dominant.
reason: The source 'seven great (noble) families' of the empire was localized as 'Seven Great Houses', matching the show's 'House' convention for noble families.
description: The seven most powerful noble houses of the Empire, standing since its founding and counted as colossi next to grassroots cultivators; their Soul Realm masters form their backbone (Ep 166). Houses Sterling and Brandt are among them, yet even their pooled resources are dwarfed by sect- and city-level powers such as the Skyreach Sect (Ep 142). Matches the source's seven great aristocratic families of the Burning Sky Dynasty, which include the Zhuge Family.

name: Raw Vitality
issues: Possible split localization: the source term 'Genuine Qi' appears rendered as 'Life Energy' in early episodes (18-135) but as 'Raw Vitality' from Ep 156 onward - Ep 164's 'Corrupt Vitality usually swallows any other Raw Vitality' directly mirrors the source's Heavenly Devil Genuine Qi devouring other types of Genuine Qi.
reason: The source energy term 'Genuine Qi' was localized as 'Raw Vitality', marking it as the cruder precursor to refined, pure Vitality in the adaptation's energy scheme.
description: The unrefined grade of a cultivator's energy: the shift from Raw Vitality to pure Vitality is described as a massive upgrade (Ep 169), and leaps in power are credited to Raw Vitality rather than brute physical strength (Ep 191). Corrupt Vitality swallows any other Raw Vitality it touches (Ep 164), and Tia is left little more than a ghost when most of her Raw Vitality is stolen (Ep 760).

name: Dread Place
reason: The source 'Fear Demon Sacred Ground', twin to the Flame Demon Sacred Ground, was localized as 'Dread Place' to pair with 'Flaming Place'.
description: One of the two peak sixth-grade sanctuaries of the Ogres, twin to the Flaming Place and the other half of the source's Twin Demon Holy Land. The pair constantly scheme for dominance, and together they declare open war on the Violet Heart Sanctuary, sending their Soul Sea Realm masters marching on its territory (Eps 601-627+).

name: Cheryl
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Cheryl' was chosen for the green-clad saint-level swordswoman of the Demon Night.
description: A saint-level genius of the Demon Night and a legend in her own right, counted with Boris among the strongest warriors on the Tower of Sin's tenth floor (Eps 602-692). Though a junior, she steps into the arena to call out the seat-holder Malcolm when he breaks the Tower's challenge rules to kill Zane, after having wagered and lost heavily on Zane's earlier fights. Matches source Mu Qingyang, the green-robed junior of the Fiend Night Clan who confronts the seat controller Meng Chong and duels Luo Zheng with shadow techniques.

name: Ethereal City
reason: The source 'Void Sky City' (also rendered 'Virtual Sky City') was renamed 'Ethereal City' for a smoother Western fantasy register.
description: A massive city of the Central Domain and home of House Kensington, one of its great noble houses (Eps 689-970). Zane arrives there as a newcomer learning its customs, and the city's noble politics and Cora's dilemma dominate the arc around Eps 689-700. Matches the source Void Sky City, seat of the Xi Family Castle and the Void Spirit Sect's influence.

name: Delroy
issues: Possible merge: Delroy's barrier feats match source Qing Feng, whose barrier is shattered by Luo Zheng (chs ~905-930), but his Ep 926 line that 'the Mark only requires the second row' corresponds to Yu Ze's Talent Stele remark in the source; two source characters may have been folded into Delroy.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized; 'Delroy' was assigned to the barrier-wielding expert of the spire expedition party.
description: A powerful warrior in the party investigating the Tower of Crystal (Eps 917-1154), known for raising and lowering enchanted barriers; Zane uses the power locked inside the Black Star to smash one of Delroy's barriers to pieces (Ep 924). He is versed in the Mark and the Tower's lore, and he leads the way to the hundred-foot tear in reality before sealing the rift behind them (Eps 928-929).

name: Francis Carter
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name, 'Francis Carter', fitting the adaptation's Western naming for named side characters.
description: Zane's thrall, bound by a slave seal and trailing silently behind him (Eps 778-807), who briefs Zane on the York Divine Kingdom and the rest of the Union as they travel and helps him fabricate a cover identity. Matches source Cao Junfeng, who as Luo Zheng's slave guides him through the customs of the four Divine Nations and the Martial Palace after narrowly escaping death in the Central Domain.

name: Celestial Law
reason: The source concept 'Heavenly Dao' (also rendered 'Heavenly Way') was localized as 'Celestial Law', stripping the Daoist term for a Western audience.
description: The underlying law of the world that cultivators comprehend and weave into strikes, forged weapons, and protections (Eps 99-1317). Threads of Celestial Law empower techniques, the Eyes of Rebirth draw on inherited rather than cultivated Celestial Law (Ep 1182), and legend holds that the ancient tribes' witchcraft aligned with it to steal a piece of Heavenly Destiny (Ep 1263).

name: Life Energy
issues: See 'Raw Vitality': the same source term 'Genuine Qi' appears localized as both 'Life Energy' (Eps 18-135) and 'Raw Vitality' (Eps 156+).
reason: The source 'Genuine Qi' was localized as 'Life Energy' for the energy used below Nature Level, converting to 'Life Force' at the Nature Level breakthrough, per the show's canon energy scheme.
description: The basic cultivation energy of characters below Nature Level (Eps 18-135): it fuels techniques like Divine Thunder, depletes rapidly with use, and leaves a cultivator too weak to lift a finger when it sputters out (Ep 22). Breaking through to Nature Level requires converting Life Energy into Life Force (Ep 107), mirroring the source's Genuine Qi-to-Genuine Essence transition.

name: Human
reason: The source 'Human Race'/'Human Clan' was carried over literally, with 'Human(s)' used as the race name among the fourteen great races.
description: One of the fourteen great races, lacking the inborn strength of Demons or Ogres but possessing remarkable potential for greatness (Eps 300, 416). Humans lean into true cultivation, channeling Vitality through their cores, and have established their own sacred place, the Violet Heart Sanctuary, in the continent's far north (Eps 568, 1210).

name: Human Alliance
reason: The source faction name 'Human Alliance' was carried over unchanged.
description: One of the great factions of the human race appearing in the final arcs (Eps 1207-1320); in the source it is named alongside two other human factions watching the late-stage conflicts. It is an organization distinct from the Human race entity and is kept separate.

name: Sword Step
reason: The source technique 'Sword Steps' was singularized to 'Sword Step' for the adaptation.
description: A famed sword-movement technique powered by the user's own sword intent; its fixed length makes it inflexible, yet its dizzying flurry of intricate moves is nearly impossible to master on the fly (Eps 248-249). Finn executes it with masterful precision to immobilize opponents, and every swordsman dreams of creating their own Sword Step. In the source it is the 'Sword Steps' comprehended by Hua Tianming.

name: Wind Law
reason: The source 'Law of Wind' was reordered to 'Wind Law' to match the adaptation's 'X Law' naming for the elemental laws.
description: One of the elemental Original Laws that cultivators comprehend in levels (Eps 459-1093). Zane masters the complete Wind Law (Ep 496), later wielding its fourth level alongside the Thunder Law and pushing it through his Chaos Energy to multiply his flight speed (Eps 1050-1058).

name: Hall of Arms
reason: The source 'Divine Weapon Hall' was renamed 'Hall of Arms' for a cleaner Western register.
description: The weapon repository of the Thirteen Palaces, where everyone who enters the Palaces gets one free weapon pick (Ep 1044). It receives shipments of Grade-One Divine-Class weapons and draws crowds of warriors; Zane lingers at its entrance sizing up the hall before claiming his pick (Eps 1045-1046). Matches the source Divine Weapon Hall of the Misty Cloud Heavenly Palace, from which even elders borrow and return weapons.

name: Castermere County
reason: The source 'Chongyang County' was renamed 'Castermere County' to fit the Western fantasy setting.
description: Zane's home region in the Eastern Territory and the seat of House Lowell, once the county's most powerful family before its fall from grace (Eps 1-20). Five powerful families - Hawthorne, Stone, Carter, Hill, and Blackwood - dominate it, and Zane returns there for revenge in Eps 326+, when the man called the 'Blood Prisoner' casts a shadow of terror across the county and its neighbors.

name: House Sterling
reason: The source's Zhuge Family, one of the empire's seven great families, was localized as 'House Sterling' under the show's 'House X' convention with a prestigious English surname.
description: One of the Seven Ruling Families of the Empire, a power since the Empire began (Ep 101). Zane's bitter feud with the house starts when he kills one of its military advisors, a vendetta pursued chiefly by Preston, the house's disciple ranked second at Stormcrown Peak (Eps 118-141). Matches the source Family Zhuge of the Burning Sky Dynasty, whose slain descendant sparks the same grudge against Luo Zheng.

name: Sacred Weapon
issues: Name drift: the show's canon declares the tier-4 weapon class 'Sacred Arms', but the delivered episodes use 'Sacred Weapon' in 19 episodes (Eps 217-1130) versus 'Sacred Arms' in only 2 (Eps 4, 70).
reason: The source tier term 'Saint Artifact' is canonically localized as 'Sacred Arms' (tier 4) per the show's weapon-tier decisions; 'Sacred Weapon' is a drifted variant of the same tier used in most episodes.

name: Master Jasper
reason: The source title-name 'Elder Xu' was localized as 'Master Jasper', a Western master's name befitting a senior sect figure.
description: A senior master of the Skyreach Sect with Core Apprentices of his own, first seen enforcing the sect's rules at the examination (Ep 40). He later appraises Zane's rare finds, staggered by the immense aura of a bone he cannot identify as Drake (Eps 288-290), and his strength is cited alongside Sir Kenneth's as the benchmark Zane must surpass in the Cloud Hall (Ep 285). Matches source Elder Xu, the mentor of Tianyi Peak, strongest of the sect's 33 peaks, whose chapter range (35-336) tracks Jasper's episode range (40-349).
